pairs.difference: A planet: a soft, nearly frontal light. There is one round hot spot at upper left and the shade fades gently to the lower right. The sphere has no dark core shadow and little difference between its lit and shadow sides, which matches the soft lesson fakes. B flippers: strong light from the upper left, with dark undersides on the foot pockets and a clear shadow side on the blade rims. Its numbers are over the real range, but real cards also go over sometimes.
pairs.fix: Light the planet from the upper left. Put a clear darker band on the lower-right part of the ball, with a slightly cooler edge just inside the outline. Let the ring cast a thin soft shadow across the ball below it.

pairs.difference: A target and bear: warm light from the overhead bulbs, a soft shadow behind the bear, and the target's side edge turning to shadow. B ice tray: light from the left, a darker right side on each cup, and a soft shadow on the table. Both have believable direction and shadow depth.

A rocket: one bright stripe down the middle of the body and the fins evenly lit. The light hits it almost head-on, and the body does not turn into a real shadow side. B submarine: light from the upper left, a broad sheen on the hull top, a darker lower-right belly, and darker rims around the portholes.
pairs.fix: Light the rocket from the upper left. Put the shine on the left third of the body and let the right side turn into a deeper blue-grey shadow. Make the far fin darker than the near fin.

pairs.difference: A robot: soft, flat light from the front. The head, chest and legs all sit at about the same grey, with only small shadows on the right sides. Its range of light to dark is below the real minimum. B gloves: the light comes from the left and wraps around the round forms, with deep shadow under the gloves and in the folds of the thumb.
pairs.fix: Light the robot from the upper left. Make the right faces of the head box, body and legs clearly darker than the front faces. Add dark contact shadows under the feet and under the head where it meets the neck.

pairs.difference: B is the real computer from the lessons: the monitor's right side drops into a cool dark-blue shadow. A alien: light from the top front. The ball body darkens evenly toward the bottom, with no side that clearly turns away from the light. The cast shadow on the floor is soft and spread out.
pairs.fix: Light the alien from the upper left. Make the right side of the body roll into a darker, slightly cool shadow, and make the shadows under the legs and the floor contact darker.

pairs.difference: A slide: clear light from one side. The slide throws a shadow onto the poles, and the curved underside of the tube is dark. B beach ball: the shading follows the colors of the panels more than the round shape. The light is broad with a weak drop-off, and its light-to-dark range is below the real range.
pairs.fix: Shade the ball as one round shape lit from the upper left. Every panel should get darker toward the lower right, whatever its color, and a firm dark contact shadow should sit where the ball touches the sand.

pairs.difference: A bus: a low key light from the left side, so the front face is in shadow, with a long dark shadow under the bus. B pod: even, near-frontal light. There is one broad sheen on the upper left of the sphere and only a mild darkening at the bottom right. The orange lights reflect on the floor, but the sphere has no clear shadow side or dark core.
pairs.fix: Make the pod sphere turn clearly darker on its right and lower half, with a darker core band before a faint purple rim. Put a dark contact shadow under the legs.

pairs.difference: A vending machine: soft purple light from the left, with the side panel gently darker. B control panel: harsh light on hard-edged boxes. The front face is uniform grey, the sloped top is bright, and the steel table has sharp reflections. Its light-to-dark range is above the real maximum.
pairs.fix: Use one soft key light from the upper left. Keep the top plane lightest, the front a step darker and the right side darkest, and blend the corners softly. Tone down the hard reflections on the table to a soft contact shadow.

pairs.difference: A jacket: light from the top, with deep darkening into the sleeves and the hem. B helmet: soft frontal light with a big glossy visor highlight. The shell barely turns into shadow on the left and right, and the shading takes on the orange of the background.
pairs.fix: Light the helmet from the upper left. Let the right half of the shell and the ear disc fall into a clear cooler shadow, and darken the inside of the neck ring.

pairs.difference: A rover: hard sunlight. There are sharp, very dark cast shadows under the wheels and deck, and the matte grey faces are flat. Its form contrast and light bias are far above the real range. B boat: soft light from the top left. The inside of the hull gets gradually darker, with soft shadows from the rope and the pier post.
pairs.fix: Soften the light on the rover. Make the shadows under the deck and wheels a soft medium dark with blurred edges. Round the shading on the tires and seats so they turn gradually from light to dark.

pairs.difference: A music player: light from the upper left, a darker right side on the rounded case, and a soft shadow behind the cable. B UFO: a broad metallic sheen across the center of the saucer, with the dome lit from the front. The rim gets darker, but the lighting has no clear direction.
pairs.fix: Light the saucer from the upper left. Put a bright sheen on the left part of the top and let the right and the underside fall into a deep cool shadow. Put one small sharp highlight on the dome.

pairs.difference: A space station: flat frontal light. The panels and cylinders are lit evenly, and there is almost no shadow side on the central sphere. Its light bias is below the real minimum. B tiki bar: light from the upper left, a darker shadow under the roof overhang, and stools that turn into shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the station from the upper left. Make the sphere and cylinders turn darker on their lower-right sides, and let the panels cast faint shadows onto the body.

pattern: Generated cards are lit almost head-on, or lit evenly with one broad sheen across the middle. Their forms have a weak shadow side and no cool dark core shadow. On the real cards, the side faces drop into a deep cool shadow under a light from the upper left. When generated cards do commit to a direction, the shadows come out too hard and black, like the rover. Their shading also tends to follow the local color or the background tint instead of the shape.
